about: A town that switched off its lamps

lines.text: Three years ago, a small coastal town decided to switch off half its street lamps.
The council’s aim was to save money, so the result surprised everyone. Within
lines.note: Connector: the result was not what the council aimed for — a contrast, 'but'.

lines.text: months, residents reported that they are sleeping better than they had in years.
lines.note: Tense: 'reported' is in the past, so it is 'were sleeping'.

lines.text: Birds that had avoided the town for decades returned to nest along the shore.
Most striking of all was the night sky. Children who had grown up
under an orange glow could now see thousands of stars by the first time.
lines.note: Preposition: it is 'for the first time'.

lines.text: Not everyone was convince. Some shopkeepers feared that darker streets would invite crime,
despite police records showed no increase in the two years that followed.
lines.note: Connector: before a full clause it is 'although'; 'despite' needs a noun.

lines.text: Other towns have since copied the idea, drawn by the save in electricity
lines.note: Word form: after 'the' a noun is needed — 'savings'.

lines.text: bills. The lesson is not that light is harm, but that we often
lines.note: Word form: after 'is' an adjective is needed — 'harmful'.

lines.text: use far more from it than we need. Darkness, it turns out,
is something worth protecting, and it costs nothing at all.
